cards.title: Welcome to Brink
body: It's the 2030s. Seven powers compete for the world's swing states: the United States, China, the European Union, Russia, India, Japan and the Gulf.
You'll play the United States. This tutorial takes about ten minutes, and every move you make in it is resolved by the real rules.

cards.title: Your homes
body: Washington, Texas and California are your homes, printed in your blue. Each is a supply centre, and centres pay for units: the more you hold, the bigger your forces.
Your three starting units stand on them.

cards.title: Swing states
body: The buff provinces are the twenty swing states. Nobody owns them at the start.
Win them over and they become your supply centres too. Hold nine at once and you win outright. Near you: Mexico, Brazil and the Southern Cone.

cards.title: Two layers of power
body: Units come in two layers. Military: the Army and the Fleet. Civil: the Capital (money) and Influence (people and media).
Every land province has two slots, one military and one civil, so two units can share it. Military units stop each other; civil units stop each other; the two layers pass through each other.

cards.title: How a year runs
body: Each year has a Spring and a Fall. Every power writes orders in secret, then they all resolve at once. Then comes Winter, when swing states change hands and everyone builds.
The turn record across the top is the game's clock. A game runs to 2040.

chapters.title: Your first move

say: Military units can't enter a swing state until it's aligned, so money and influence go in first.
Your Capital in California can move straight into Mexico.
S2031M.task: Move your Capital from California into Mexico.

guide.text: Click your Capital in California: the counter with stacked ingots, marked USA.
The places it can go are hatched in red. Click Mexico.
That's your order, drawn in red. Press Commit orders.

say: Nothing threatens Mexico this Fall. A unit with no order simply holds where it is.
F2031M.task: Commit with no new orders: everything holds.

guide.text: Press Commit orders.

say: Winter. A swing state aligns to whoever holds both its slots, or one slot with the other empty. Your Capital alone has aligned Mexico: it's now your supply centre, tinted blue.
Four centres, three units: you build one new unit at home.
W2031A.task: Build one unit at a home with a free slot.

guide.text: Click California on the map, then choose a unit to build there in the panel. Leave the nuclear umbrellas as they are: more on those later.
Press Commit to finish the Winter.

S2031M.success: Your Capital is in Mexico. At the same moment, Europe's Capital crossed the Atlantic on a trade route into Brazil. Nobody saw anyone's orders until they resolved: that's the heart of the game.
S2031M.miss: Your Capital didn't reach Mexico this time. Replay the lesson and move it there.

W2031A.success: Mexico is yours and you have a new unit. That's the loop of Brink: move in, align, build, grow.
W2031A.miss: Mexico didn't align to you. Replay the lesson to see it happen.

chapters.done: You aligned your first swing state and built with it.

chapters.title: Standoffs and support

say: This time Brazil is empty, and Europe wants it as much as you do.
Every unit in Brink has the same strength. When two try to enter the same place at once, the stronger side gets in.
S2032M.task: Move your Capital from Texas into Brazil, along the South Atlantic trade route.

guide.text: Click your Capital in Texas.
Click Brazil.
Press Commit orders.

say: To win a contest you need more strength than the other side. Any unit can support another unit's move, from either layer, as long as it could move there itself.
Your Influence in the Andes is right next to Brazil.
F2032M.task: Order Texas into Brazil again, with your Influence in the Andes supporting it.

guide.text: First the move: click your Capital in Texas, then Brazil.
Now click your Influence in the Andes: the counter with broadcast arcs.
Press S, or choose Support in the slip at the top of the map.
Click the unit you're supporting: your Capital in Texas.

guide.until: order:I AND S C TEX - BRA
guide.text: Click Brazil, the destination you're supporting.
Two orders, one plan. Press Commit orders.

solution: I AND S C TEX - BRA

say: Winter: Brazil aligns to you. Five centres and three units means two builds.
W2032A.task: Build up to two units, then commit.

guide.text: Click one of your homes, then choose a unit in the panel.
Add a second build if you like, then press Commit. Builds you don't use are lost.

S2032M.success: A standoff. Europe's Capital tried for Brazil too: one against one, so both bounced and Brazil stays empty. The crossed box on each arrow marks a move that failed.
S2032M.miss: You got into Brazil first time, so you must have brought support. That's exactly the trick the next turn teaches.

F2032M.success: Two against one: your Capital took Brazil and Europe's bounced off. Support is how every contest in Brink is won.
F2032M.miss: Brazil held out. Replay the lesson and give the move its support.

chapters.done: You won a contest with support. Plans that need two units are the core of good play.

chapters.title: Both slots

say: Mexico is aligned to you now, and an aligned state is open to Armies and Fleets.
With a unit in each slot, a rival has to dislodge one of yours to break in. A swing state with a rival unit inside is contested: it pays you nothing until you clear it out.
S2033M.task: Move your Army from Texas into Mexico's military slot.

guide.text: Click your Army in Texas: the box with a cross.
Click Mexico.
Press Commit orders.

S2033M.success: Both of Mexico's slots are yours: an Army and a Capital side by side. That's a state that's hard to take.
S2033M.miss: The Army didn't arrive. Replay the lesson and move it into Mexico.

chapters.done: Hold both slots and your states are safe.

cards.title: The Crisis track
body: One track is shared by everyone. It rises every year (faster from 2036) and with every closed chokepoint and every war between nuclear powers.
At 6 everyone builds one fewer. At 10 the world collapses and every power scores zero. Commons orders bring it down: cooperation is part of winning.

cards.title: Nuclear homes
body: Five powers are nuclear: their homes can never be attacked, so rivalry plays out in the swing states.
Japan and the Gulf aren't nuclear. They shelter under American umbrellas, which you can withdraw in secret.

cards.title: Chokepoints and special orders
body: A Fleet in a chokepoint like Hormuz or Malacca can close it to rivals, cutting their trade routes, at a cost to the Crisis track.
Capitals can sanction a rival, Influence can disrupt a rival's support from two provinces away, and any unit can work for the Commons.

cards.title: The Assembly
body: Each Winter the power with the fewest centres chairs the Assembly and may put a resolution to the vote: sanctions, peacekeeping, a climate accord.
Votes are weighted by swing states held, and each power has one veto for the whole game.

cards.title: Talk, then act
body: Between moves, players negotiate in private messages. Deals aren't binding: only the orders are.
Bots take any seat nobody claims, so a game can start with two friends or seven.

cards.title: Winning
body: Align nine swing states at once and you win outright. Otherwise the game ends after Winter 2040 and scores favour a clear lead.
If the Crisis track reaches 10, nobody wins.
